Needs a real re-run.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: UNVERIFIED in this second pass; earlier-scan evidence only. Trivia Flow reportedly has a free-forever tier with ready-to-play packages and automatic AI grading (E7); Trivnow is reportedly $25/month with unlimited question creation (E5); Cheap Trivia weekly pack is reportedly $1 first month then $60/month (E2); Buzztime from $199/month (E3); Geeks Who Drink about $200/night (E4); DIY with staff 4-6 hours per night (E1). No new alternatives could be searched because the search budget was exhausted.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None established. The scan-1 edge is owner/staff time saved through automation, which is not an edge by the rules, and a 'local' pack (city events, venue name, menu) can be copied by any pack seller or any venue with an LLM. A plausible compounding asset would be a curated per-city local-knowledge dataset plus venue relationships and retention data, which a stranger does not have at day 0 (inference). Falsifier: venues renew a $20-29 local pack at a clearly lower churn than generic $0-29 products; no evidence either way was found.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: UNVERIFIED. A vendor blog says most independent venues spend $30-100/month (E6) and list prices of $25-$199/month exist (E2, E3, E5), which suggests venues pay for trivia, but nobody was shown paying for a localised pack, and E6 comes from a vendor that sells packs. Churn is likely high because venues drop trivia nights (earlier-scan note).

answers.question: (4) Legal / platform constraints?
answers.answer: No platform dependency. Content rights are the open point: image and audio rounds raise copyright questions and question accuracy matters (earlier-scan note). Nothing was read in this second pass to confirm how existing pack sellers handle licensing, so treat as unverified.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers?
answers.answer: Bottom-up, built only from assumptions plus the earlier-scan model ($25/month, $6.25 variable per venue-month, $1,000 startup). Base: paying venue-months ramp 0,1,3,5,8,10,12,14,16,18,20,22 = 129 venue-months x $25 = $3,225 revenue; cost $1,000 startup + $806 variable + $600 outreach/tools ($50/month) = $2,406; profit about $819 on ~700 owner hours. Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): 64.5 venue-months x $20 = $1,290 revenue; cost (1,000+600) x1.5 + 64.5 x $9.375 = $3,005; profit about -$1,715. Does not survive pessimistic, but every volume input is an unsourced assumption and no venue-acquisition cost per sale was found.
